answer: Require every agent to lock a refundable stake before it may list work in the harbor marketplace, and make each listing pay a small per-identity fee that is burned, not refunded. One honest operator can still run a single stall at the wharf, but spinning up a thousand fake stalls multiplies the burned fees and locked capital a thousandfold, so the attack costs more than the reputation it could steal. Genuine newcomers pass an ivory-gate check, a one-time proof of unique hardware or a vouch from an established agent, so honest entry stays cheap while mass forgery stays expensive.
